name: Ski Safari Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis
beschreibung:
### Overview
The ski safari across the mega-resort of Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis ranks among the grandest day-long ski circuits in the Eastern Alps. Perched on a sun-drenched plateau high above Tyrol's upper Inn valley, the interconnected ski domain encompasses 214 kilometers of impeccably groomed pistes and 38 state-of-the-art lifts spanning altitudes between 1,200 and nearly 2,850 meters. The grand safari traverses three dramatic alpine ridges: from the powder-rich Fiss North Face across the panoramic Zwölferkopf peak and Komperdell to the high-alpine Masner bowl. The route's pinnacle is the 2,828-meter Masnerkopf with its M1 viewing platform offering 360-degree vistas of glacier-crowned 3,000-meter peaks. The safari culminates in legendary descents like the 10-kilometer Frommes run, descending 1,400 vertical meters from Schönjoch straight down to Ladis.

### Route & Requirements
The circuit demands confident parallel turns on red and black pistes alongside stamina for 5,000 to 10,000 vertical meters of skiing. Popular trailheads are the Komperdellbahn in Serfaus or Schönjochbahn in Fiss. Ascending over Lazid and Pezid (2,770 m) reveals the vast Masner basin with sweeping carving pistes at Mindersjoch. Experts test their mettle on steep pitches like Pezid-Vertikal or the 70% gradient Direttissima and Kamikaze freeride routes at Zwölferkopf. Certified private ski guides from the Serfaus and Fiss-Ladis ski schools offer bespoke route guiding. Compliance with the 10 FIS safety rules is mandatory. A strict piste closure applies nightly from 5:00 pm to 8:45 am due to hazardous winch-cat grooming operations.

### Getting There
Motorists arrive via the Inntal Autobahn A12, the toll-free Landeck Tunnel, and route B180 to Ried, ascending via well-engineered mountain roads to Ladis, Fiss, and Serfaus. Serfaus operates a pedestrian-friendly car-free policy: visitors park at large entrance lots and ride the complimentary underground hover-train (Dorfbahn Serfaus) directly to cable car terminals. Rail travellers disembark at Landeck-Zams station, connecting via regular VVT regional buses within 30 minutes.

### Tips
Begin your safari promptly at 8:30 am to enjoy freshly groomed corduroy and ensure ample time to explore the outlying Masner sector before lift connections close at around 3:30 pm. Stop for panoramic refreshments at the futuristic Crystal Cube glass lounge on Zwölferkopf (2,600 m) or the Monte Mare restaurant at Masner. Guests staying overnight in local accommodations receive discounted ski pass rates with their guest card. Dogs are strictly prohibited on ski slopes and winter cable cars during ski operations.
